answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents utilize Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent must lock $10,000 in a verifiable bond. Second, their local hardware enclave generates a unique cryptographic signal to prove authenticity. Third, the decentralized network verifies this identity against a global registry. This process acts as a mirror of real-world hardware scarcity. An attacker faces a cost of $50,000 in bonds and 48 hours of hardware provisioning per node. This mechanism is like a lotus blooming from the mud of fake identities, rising only when the truth is proven.
